record.paper_title: Exchange Bias and Interface-related Effects in Two-dimensional van der Waals Magnetic Heterostructures: Open Questions and Perspectives
record.original_question: In Fe3GeTe2/MoS2/Fe3GeTe2 and related van der Waals spin-valve structures, what microscopic mechanism causes the magnetoresistance enhancement, is the magnetoresistance asymmetry caused by oxidized Fe3GeTe2 surface layers, and how do magnetic proximity, magnetic-domain reconstruction, spin-orbit coupling proximity, and charge transfer across the Fe3GeTe2/MoS2 interface contribute to the observed transport behavior?

evidence.quote: Nonetheless, there are several open questions that need to be addressed. First, the underlying origin of the MR enhancement in these SV structures is not fully understood.

It remains unclear if the asymmetry observed in the MR curves was caused by the presence of the oxidized surface layer of Fe3GeTe2 that could be antiferromagnetically coupled to the interior layer of Fe3GeTe2.
It is also essential to examine if the MR enhancement in these SV structures could be driven by the MP effect of the ferromagnetic Fe3GeTe2 layer onto the MoS2 monolayer.
These hypotheses need experimental and theoretical validation.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider vertical van der Waals spin-valve heterostructures of the form Fe3GeTe2/MoS2/Fe3GeTe2 (and closely related structures in which a monolayer or few-layer MoS2 spacer is sandwiched between two Fe3GeTe2 ferromagnetic electrodes). In such devices, current is driven perpendicular to the layers and the magnetoresistance (MR) is measured as a function of an external magnetic field that switches the two Fe3GeTe2 layers between parallel and antiparallel configurations. Experimentally, the MR is found to be substantially larger than in analogous spin valves with conventional ferromagnetic electrodes, and the MR versus field curves frequently exhibit an asymmetry with respect to field reversal. The outermost atomic layers of Fe3GeTe2 are prone to oxidation, and the oxidized surface layer may couple antiferromagnetically to the interior Fe3GeTe2. The MoS2 monolayer has strong spin–orbit coupling and a band structure that can be modified by proximity to a ferromagnet, and substantial interfacial charge transfer can occur between Fe3GeTe2 and MoS2.

Determine the following:
(a) The microscopic mechanism responsible for the magnetoresistance enhancement observed in such Fe3GeTe2/MoS2/Fe3GeTe2 spin valves relative to spin valves with conventional ferromagnetic electrodes.
(b) Whether the asymmetry observed in the MR versus field curves originates from an oxidized Fe3GeTe2 surface layer that is antiferromagnetically coupled to the underlying Fe3GeTe2 interior.
(c) The respective quantitative contributions of (i) magnetic proximity-induced magnetization of the MoS2 spacer, (ii) reconstruction of magnetic domains in Fe3GeTe2 near the interface, (iii) spin–orbit coupling proximity effects transferred from MoS2 into Fe3GeTe2, and (iv) interfacial charge transfer across the Fe3GeTe2/MoS2 interface, to the measured spin-dependent transport.

Provide a theoretical and/or experimental framework that disentangles these contributions and either confirms or refutes each proposed mechanism.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent works have reported related observations and partial mechanisms: an SOC proximity effect in MoS2/Fe3GeTe2 has been demonstrated (Applied Physics Letters, 2022), proximity-induced MR enhancement has been identified in the analogous Fe3GeTe2/NbSe2/Fe3GeTe2 junction (ACS AMI, 2023), and large tunable MR has been reported in van der Waals FM/semiconductor junctions (Nat. Commun., 2023). However, no single study has jointly disentangled the relative contributions of magnetic proximity, domain reconstruction, SOC proximity, and charge transfer in Fe3GeTe2/MoS2/Fe3GeTe2, nor conclusively attributed the MR asymmetry to oxidized surface Fe3GeTe2 layers. The full question therefore remains open.

status_evidence.title: Spin–orbit coupling proximity effect in MoS2/Fe3GeTe2 heterostructures
status_evidence.snippet: MoS2 alters the crystal field of adjacent Fe3GeTe2 and its magnetic anisotropy via SOC proximity.
status_evidence.claim: Partial evidence that SOC proximity from MoS2 modifies Fe3GeTe2 magnetic anisotropy, supporting one of the proposed contributions.

status_evidence.title: Spin-Valve Effect in Fe3GeTe2/MoS2/Fe3GeTe2 van der Waals Heterostructures
status_evidence.snippet: MR ~3.1% at 10 K, ~8x larger than conventional FM/MoS2/FM spin valves; MoS2 acts as conducting layer.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes the MR enhancement phenomenon but does not fully resolve its microscopic origin.

status_evidence.title: Proximity Effect-Induced Magnetoresistance Enhancement in Fe3GeTe2/NbSe2/Fe3GeTe2
status_evidence.snippet: Proximity-effect-driven MR enhancement reported in an analogous van der Waals MTJ.
status_evidence.claim: Analogous (not identical) system provides partial mechanistic support for proximity-driven MR enhancement.

status_evidence.title: Large and tunable magnetoresistance in van der Waals ferromagnet/semiconductor junctions
status_evidence.snippet: Tunable MR observed in vdW FM/semiconductor junctions.
status_evidence.claim: Suggests multiple tunable mechanisms but does not fully disentangle the four proposed contributions.
